**THE AKRON DAILY BEACON**

**VOL. 1, ISSUE 1**

**JULY 3RD, 2014**

**AKRON VANISHES IN FLAMES; CITY LEFT IN RUINS**

In a bizarre and inexplicable event, the city of Akron, Ohio, has spontaneously combusted, leaving behind a smoldering crater and a population of bewildered residents who seem to have forgotten the entire ordeal.

Eyewitnesses describe the scene as "apocalyptic" and "surreal," with flames engulfing the city's skyline and a massive plume of smoke billowing into the air. "I was driving home from work when suddenly the city was on fire," said local resident, Jane Doe. "I didn't think much of it at first, but then I saw people running around, screaming, and I realized something was very wrong."

As the city burned, residents reported feeling a strange, disorienting sensation, as if they were being pulled back in time. "I remember walking out of my house and seeing people in medieval clothing," said John Smith, a local business owner. "I thought it was some kind of prank, but then I saw the trees and the buildings, and I realized it was real."

The city's landscape has returned to its pre-industrial state, with the Cuyahoga River flowing through the center of town and the surrounding hills covered in dense forests. The once-thriving metropolis is now a barren, charred expanse, devoid of any signs of human habitation.

Families who were in the city at the time of the event report having no memory of what happened. "I was at home with my kids when the fire started," said Sarah Johnson. "We just woke up the next morning, and everything was...different. The city was gone, and we had no idea what had happened."

As the city's residents struggle to come to terms with their new reality, officials are left to wonder what caused the catastrophic event. "We're stumped," said Mayor, Tom Stevens. "We've never seen anything like this before. We're working with experts to try and figure out what happened, but so far, we have no answers."

The city's disappearance has sent shockwaves throughout the nation, with many wondering if this is the end of the world as we know it. "This is a dark day for America," said Senator, John McCain. "We need to come together as a nation and support our fellow citizens who have been affected by this tragedy."

As the people of Akron struggle to rebuild their lives, one thing is clear: the city will never be the same again.
